messages:
Anya: Heads-up — around 03:10 UTC we started seeing NVMe IO saturation on mirrored pool mpool-eu1. GPU attach jobs failing and falling back to remote volumes, latency + cost spike.
Sam: Ugh. Any metrics? is it batching or janitor churn? :eyes:
Priya: Quick snapshot from the host fleet: avg await ~22ms on nvme[0-3], util ~97%, queue-len peaking 256. Kernel logs show repeated write stalls.
Priya: Example iostat line: 
```
Device:         r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme2n1        1200   3400  96000  272000   80.0    12.5   24.9   5.1   25.0   0.30  97.1
```
Raj: That matches the attach failure traces — orchestration tried 3x then fell back. Fallback path added ~120ms p99 and ~3x egress cost for those jobs.
Anya: Which component is spiking IO? janitor/cleaner or user batch writes?
Priya: Correlation shows scrub window overlap with a batch deploy wave. Janitor throughput shot up on nodes hosting hot stripes. janitor-bot logged lots of "deep-scan" tasks at 03:08.
janitor-bot: Automated note — scheduled scrub batch triggered per policy windows: 03:00-04:00 UTC for region eu1.
Sam: Short term mitigation: can we throttle janitor on mpool-eu1 and shift its tasks to cooler hosts? Also pause large batch launches for 30m?
Raj: I can push a temporary rate cap. Proposed patch: 
```
kubectl patch cm janitor-config -n infra --type merge -p '{"data":{"scrub_throttle_ms":"50"}}'
```
Raj: That should reduce per-op concurrency and drop queue depth. I'll stage to canary hosts first.
Priya: Also recommend enabling attach-local-affinity to prefer nodes with healthy nvme, and add alert rule for avgqu-sz > 8 on any nvme device.
Anya: Good. Sam, please coordinate a 30m hold on batch ramp in eu1 — I'll notify platform and sales-facing SREs.
Sam: On it, posting hold in #eng-oncall and pausing the deploy queue.
alert-bot: Alert created: NVME_AVGQU_GT_8 on mpool-eu1 (firing). Pager duty notified.
Raj: Patching janitor config to 50ms on canary hosts now. Rolling if green.
Priya: If this doesn't drop within 10m we'll consider shifting scrub window to off-peak (00:00-02:00) and throttling deep-scan heuristics. That will reduce immediate throughput but increases backlog.
Anya: Note for postmortem: we should add a policy preventing scrub + large batch on same hostset and quantify cost delta when fallback to remote volumes occurs. We saw an extra $0.02/token equivalent for the affected runs.
Sam: Agreed. Action items: throttle janitor (Raj), hold batch ramp (Sam), alert rule + affinity change (Priya), postmortem (Anya).
Raj: Patch applied to canaries, telemetry shows avgqu-sz down to ~6 on canaries after ~90s. Slower rollout now.
Anya: Nice. Keep monitoring p99 attach latency and egress cost. If anything regresses, escalate. :thumbsup:
